# Operator Note — Airborne Dust from Blasting (see SB-1026)

This note summarizes immediate actions and expectations from the safety bulletin on airborne dust hazards during blasting. Review SB-1026 in full before resuming work.

Key actions for operators
- Suspend blasting activities if visible dust escapes containment or control measures appear compromised.
- Don required respiratory protection and face/eye protection per SB-1026 before entering the blast area or adjacent work zones.
- Follow established containment procedures: verify barriers, curtains, and negative airflow systems are functioning and properly positioned.
- Limit access to the blast area to essential personnel only; post signage and communicate the hazard status to oncoming crews.

Housekeeping and cleanup
- Avoid dry sweeping in contaminated areas; use wet methods or HEPA-filtered vacuuming as specified in the bulletin.
- Collect and handle residues as potentially hazardous material; use labeled, covered containers and transfer through designated routes.

Reporting and follow-up
- Report any breach of controls, equipment failure, or suspected overexposure immediately to supervision and safety.
- Document incidents and corrective actions in the site log; schedule equipment inspection and requalification as required by SB-1026.

Health and monitoring
- If symptoms of respiratory irritation or other health concerns occur, remove the affected person to fresh air and seek medical evaluation.
- Participate in any follow-up monitoring or medical surveillance prompted by incidents or repeated exposures.

Remain vigilant. Adherence to the bulletin protects you and your coworkers.
